Funnel.io, Coupler.io, Fivetran, Airbyte, and Supermetrics all do the same basic thing: move data between systems. That is where the similarity stops. Some are built around marketing data and reporting. Others make more sense when the destination is a data warehouse, or when your team wants control over the pipeline itself.

Picking data integration software isn't a matter of counting connectors. It's about the path your data needs to take. Three questions narrow the field fast:

- Where does the data come from?
- How much transformation does it need?
- Where does it need to land?

{{% tldr %}}
Five tools, four different jobs. Funnel and Supermetrics are marketing-first, with data models built around ad platforms and reporting destinations. Coupler.io spans a wider mix of business sources (400+ across marketing, sales, ecommerce, and finance) and starts at $24/month against Funnel's $300. Fivetran is the managed, warehouse-first option with 750+ sources, change data capture, and automatic schema handling. Airbyte is the open-source one: 600+ connectors, custom connectors when yours isn't in the catalog, and self-hosting if you'd rather own the infrastructure than outsource it. Start from your sources, your destination, and how much of the plumbing you want to run.
{{% /tldr %}}

## Funnel.io vs. Coupler.io: start with the workflow

Funnel is the natural pick when marketing data dominates the pipeline. Its connector catalog covers hundreds of platforms, with built-in field mapping, custom dimensions and metrics, normalisation, and currency conversion applied before anything reaches a dashboard or warehouse.

The overlap with {{< link href="https://www.coupler.io/" >}}Coupler.io{{< /link >}} is substantial, which is why it's one of the more affordable Funnel io alternatives at the entry level. The scope is different, though. Coupler.io pulls from more than 400 sources across marketing, sales, ecommerce, finance, and other business functions. A single flow can combine those sources and apply filters and formulas, then send the result to Google Sheets, Excel, Looker Studio, and other supported destinations. That difference in scope matters more than the raw connector count.

A marketing team running dozens of ad accounts gets real value from Funnel's marketing-specific data model. A smaller analytics team joining Facebook Ads to Shopify, QuickBooks, and a spreadsheet will find more of those sources covered by Coupler.io.

Price separates them quickly too. Funnel's Starter plan begins at $300 per month billed annually. Coupler.io has a free tier, and paid plans start at $24 per month with annual billing. At larger scales the headline number matters less than connector limits, refresh frequency, account counts, and destination requirements.

## Alternatives to Funnel and Coupler.io worth considering

Those two aren't the only options. Both can send data to a warehouse, but the requirements change when the warehouse is the center of the stack. Warehouse-first pipelines usually follow an {{< link href="https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-elt" >}}ELT model{{< /link >}}: extract the data, load it into the target system, and transform it there.

Some of the best data integration tools take a different approach, particularly when the pipeline ends in a warehouse or needs more engineering control.

### Fivetran: good for warehouse-first pipelines

Fivetran is the stronger fit when the main job is replicating data into a warehouse, lake, or database. It currently supports more than 750 sources across SaaS applications, databases, event streams, and files, and handles incremental syncs, API changes, and schema changes on its own.

That managed approach cuts pipeline maintenance. Fivetran owns most of the replication plumbing, including schema drift and incremental updates. For supported databases it can use change data capture to replicate changes instead of copying whole tables on every run. The flip side is giving up control. Teams that want to run the integration infrastructure themselves will find Airbyte more flexible.

### Airbyte: when you want more control

Airbyte is the open-source option, and it runs either as cloud or self-managed. The catalog has more than 600 replication connectors, and your team can build its own when an integration isn't there. That matters for internal APIs and for less common SaaS products that never show up in a vendor's connector list.

Self-managed deployment gives engineering teams control over infrastructure and data movement. The tradeoff is that the same team now deploys, upgrades, monitors, and troubleshoots it.

### Supermetrics: for marketing reporting

Supermetrics stays closer to Funnel's territory. It supports more than 100 data source connectors with a heavy focus on advertising and analytics, and data can go straight into reporting destinations or into warehouses and cloud storage.

It's the right call when the problem is specifically marketing reporting rather than general-purpose data integration. A team mainly moving advertising and analytics data into Google Sheets doesn't need the warehouse-first workflow that makes Fivetran and Airbyte attractive.

## Match the tool to your stack

Across all five, there's no single winner to recommend.

- Funnel and Supermetrics make sense when marketing data dominates the pipeline.
- Coupler.io covers a broader mix of business reporting sources at a lower entry price.
- Fivetran fits managed, warehouse-first pipelines.
- Airbyte is worth a look when engineering control matters more than minimising infrastructure work.

Start with the sources, the destination, and the level of control your team actually wants. Connector count comes second. The decision usually falls out of those three answers on its own.
